Disagree with this article completely and the arguments for it are weak.

The lifespan of consoles hasn't been shrinking, it's been getting longer. The PS4 Pro and the Xbox One X aren't new consoles, they are hardware revisions which have been common in the console business for decades. It gives you a mid-life boost in sales. Every single console since '79 has done this. It gives you the opportunity to get free press from news sites, excite your base, and get your older products into the hands of new consumers with a price drop. Par for the course.

Console games are now built on top of middleware that is scalable to multiple platforms. All of the AAA developers have their own engines that scale, and the vast majority of indie games use an engine that allows them to put out their game on more devices. This is smart from a business sense. Now you can create your game for a specific platform, but it can be ported with (relative to the past) ease and maximize your market penetration. This is why you are seeing franchises that used to be exclusive to consoles now coming to PC. No longer does a game have to be made for a specific instruction set architecture, which was a big hurdle in the past. Now consoles use the same architecture as most common PC's, which basically makes them PC towers that are designed to sit in your living room. This has also led to the increase of games getting released on everything.

Now as far as first-party Microsoft developers releasing their biggest franchises on "Games for Windows", a large part of that has to do with Microsoft board members hating the Xbox division. They want to kill it, and make no secret of it in investor relation meetings. The game market is more volatile and costs too many dollars up-front with fingers crossed that it pays off. Microsoft not only dominates the PC desktop market, but they also own DirectX and a game distribution store for desktops. So it makes since that they are putting their games up on PC stores, those games are already designed to run on a PC. The Xbox is a PC.
